text:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH - kvcache OOMs in hosted-runtime (svc: runtime-hosted, impact: latency/errors)
ops-bot: Incident channel created -> #incidents (ops-3380001111)
maria: paging @oncall, I'm seeing KV cache mem spike on prod-gpu-4 in eu-west-1, multiple OOMs and reconnects. traces point to very long prompts causing runaway context windows.
jon: oncall here, joining. what's the customer impact?
emily: CX report: 3 customers seeing 5xxs and slow completions, backlog growing on hosted-api. one reported suddenly truncated generations.
sanjay: logs: ```
2026-03-15T02:13:07Z runtime-hosted[pid=4321] ERROR: kvcache: alloc failed, OOM, alloc=3.2GB free=200MB
2026-03-15T02:13:08Z runtime-hosted[pid=4321] WARN: continuous-batcher: batch size ballooned to 128 due to long sequence prefix
2026-03-15T02:13:09Z runtime-hosted[pid=4321] ERROR: session 0x7f4d context length 1.2M tokens
```
maria: wow 1.2M tokens. looks like prefix amplification + continuous batching + no prefetch cap. heating up.
ryan: quick mitigation idea: disable continuous batching at the frontend routing level for hosted tier and set prefetch cap to 32KB per session. we can push a hotfix to the runtime config.
jon: agree. prioritise: 1) throttle prefetch, 2) disable continuous batching, 3) evict oversized KV entries, 4) notify customers. who can push runtime config?
sanjay: I can patch the routing flag and deploy a config change to disable continuous batching in 60s. preparing patch.
emily: I'll open the customer impact matrix and notify affected accounts. cc @customer-success for direct outreach.
maria: also want a short-term kernel-level guard: force-evict paths > 256k tokens to avoid single session blowups.
jon: sanjay, go ahead with config, but hold kernel changes until we validate. let's do a staged rollout region-by-region starting eu-west-1.
sanjay: deploying: ```
curl -X POST https://config.internal/api/v1/flags -d '{"service":"runtime-hosted","flag":"continuous_batching","value":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'```
ops-bot: deploybot: rollout started for runtime-hosted flags in eu-west-1 (change-id: cfg-20260315-01).
10m later
ops-bot: deploybot: rollout succeeded in eu-west-1.
jon: confirm metrics? maria, can you watch KV cache mem graphs?
maria: mem usage dropped ~40% on the affected hosts, error rate down from 7% -> 1.2% in eu-west-1. backlog shrinking.
ryan: pushing prefetch cap hotfix now to 32KB/session: ```
kubectl exec -n runtime config-api -- curl -X PATCH http://localhost/flags -d '{"prefetch_per_session_bytes":32768}'
```
ops-bot: change accepted, new prefetch cap rolling to hosted runtime.
emily: customer updates sent: templated note + targeted outreach started.
customer-success: customer A acknowledged, their jobs resumed, asked for root cause and ETA on fix.
jon: OK, now plan for medium-term: add per-session kv size guards, telemetry for session prefix amplification, and automated prefetch backpressure for long contexts. create RFC and ship in two sprints.
maria: also propose an emergency regression test: synthetic long prompt generator to exercise kvcache and batching.
ryan: logging follow-ups: capture a sample of offending prompts (scrubbed) for analysis. we'll need to mask PII.
sanjay: I'm going to evict large entries from nodes where mem > 90% to avoid recurrence: `kvcache-ctrl evict --threshold 0.9 --max-evict 1000`
ops-bot: kvcache-ctrl: evict job started, progress 0/1000
20m later
ops-bot: kvcache-ctrl: evict job completed 968/1000 entries evicted.
maria: eviction freed ~55GB across cluster, no additional OOMs observed. good.
jon: handoff: I'm documenting the mitigations in the incident tracker and will hand over to oncall for night watch. last check in 30m.
emily: logged customer impact, created follow-up tasks: CS-4321 (customer outreach), ENG-4322 (prefetch/backpressure), ENG-4323 (eviction guard), ENG-4324 (longprompt test harness).
customer-success: flagged one high-importance account for SLA credit discussion.
ryan: root-cause hypothesis: continuous batching + lack of prefetch caps + prefix amplification in some prompt templates -> KV entries grew without bound. combination triggered per-process OOMs.
maria: agree. also see a regression in batching logic from last week's runtime change that relaxed max-batch token heuristics. adding that to RCA.
jon: final operational notes for the rest of the oncall team: - keep continuous_batching disabled for hosted-prod until next deploy that includes backpressure. - monitor kvcache_free_bytes and session_kv_size histograms. - alert if session_kv_size > 500k tokens or if per-host free < 300MB.
sanjay: created a short hotpatch PR to reintroduce a hard max-batch-token cap. link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/7890
emily: I'm scheduling a post-incident review tomorrow 1500 UTC, invite sent.
jon: thanks all. closing primary pager. will reopen if we see regressions. :white_check_mark:
